Title: Evaluation of a Cumulus Scheme in the FV3-LAM and of Experimental MPAS Forecasts for the Summer 2025 Flash Flood and Intense Rainfall Experiment
Proposed Project Title: FV3-LAM CAM Ensemble Forecast System and Improving Ensemble Probabilistic and Consensus Forecast Products in Support of HMT Winter Weather and Heavy Precipitation Forecasting
Suggested Parent Project: FV3-LAM CAM Ensemble Forecast System and Improving Ensemble Probabilistic and Consensus Forecast Products in Support of HMT Winter Weather and Heavy Precipitation Forecasting
Authors / PI: Andrew H. Berrington; Nathan Snook; Ming Xue; Bryan Carroll; Keith A. Brewster; Sarah Trojniak; James Correia
Brief Abstract: Abstract A convection-allowing model (CAM) ensemble was run during the NOAA Hydrometeorological Testbed’s 2025 Flash Flood and Intense Rainfall Experiment. One of the goals was to evaluate the role and effects of a cumulus scheme on precipitation forecasting in CAMs, where four members of the ensemble have a scale-aware simplified Arakawa–Schubert (saSAS) cumulus scheme activated, while the other four have it turned off. The ensemble was run once daily for the 24 days of the experiment. The ensemble consisted of eight Finite-Volume Cubed-Sphere Limited Area Model (FV3-LAM) members and three experimental Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) members run on 3-km grids and employed a variety of physics combinations.
